Because Busy Beaver is interested in statistics, he wants to control the frequencies of letters appearing in words, so he has chosen a multiset a$$$a$$$ of size NM$$$NM$$$ of letters from his alphabet. He will now form N$$$N$$$ words each with M$$$M$$$ letters such that each letter from a$$$a$$$ is used exactly once (i.e. if a given letter x$$$x$$$ appears exactly k$$$k$$$ times in a$$$a$$$, then it is used exactly k$$$k$$$ times across all N$$$N$$$ words).

After forming the words, Busy Beaver plans to organize them into a dictionary, so he will lexicographically sort his N$$$N$$$ words to produce the sequence of words s1,…,sN$$$s_1, \ldots, s_N$$$. Busy Beaver likes strings to be lexicographically small, so for each k$$$k$$$ from 1$$$1$$$ to N$$$N$$$ he wants to know the lexicographically minimum possible value of sk$$$s_k$$$ over all choices of words.
Note that the answer for each sk$$$s_k$$$ is independent; for example, the choice of words so that s1$$$s_1$$$ is minimized may be different from the choice of words so that s2$$$s_2$$$ is minimized.
